evidence: Tony Visconti is credited as producer on David Bowie's 'Young Americans' (1975) and, alongside Brian Eno, on 'Low' and '"Heroes"' (both 1977), and has discussed the decades-long working relationship extensively in his own memoir and in interviews.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Young Americans' is Visconti working in a horn-driven, American soul idiom. Two years later, at Hansa Studios in Berlin, the same producer is building a title track around Robert Fripp's treated guitar and Eno's synthesizer textures. Same producer, same artist, almost unrecognizably different palette.

explanation.age7: Tony Visconti produced David Bowie's records for many years, including ones made in a soul style and later ones made in Berlin.
explanation.age13: Visconti produced Bowie's 'Young Americans' (1975) and, with Brian Eno, 'Low' and '"Heroes"' (1977), covering a huge stylistic range across one working partnership.
explanation.adult: The Visconti-Bowie relationship, on and off across decades, is one of this dataset's clearest examples of a producer partnership outlasting any single genre both people passed through.
